project_id: MiniDOGE Smart Contract Audit Report - QuillAudits

preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to trigger Sweep() function, or marketingAddress must be a contract with gas-intensive fallback
Contract must have ETH balance to transfer

violation_target.exploit_hint: The vulnerability exists in transferToAddressETH() which uses recipient.transfer(amount) with hardcoded 2300 gas limit. To exploit: 1) If attacker controls marketingAddress, deploy a contract with fallback function requiring >2300 gas. 2) Trigger swapTokens() which calls transferToAddressETH(marketingAddress, ...). 3) The transfer will fail, causing the entire transaction to revert, potentially DoSing the swap/liquidity mechanism. Alternatively, owner can call Sweep() which also uses .transfer() to send ETH to owner address.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The MiniDOGE contract has an unsafe Ether transfer vulnerability in two functions: 1) `transferToAddressETH()` uses `recipient.transfer(amount)` which has a hardcoded 2300 gas limit, and 2) `Sweep()` uses `payable(owner()).transfer(balance)` with the same limitation. If the recipient is a contract with a gas-intensive fallback/receive function, the transfer will fail and revert the entire transaction. This can be exploited to DoS the swap/liquidity mechanism or prevent the owner from sweeping funds.
attempts.attack_strategy: Deploy an attacker contract with a gas-intensive fallback function (>2300 gas). Impersonate the contract owner to set marketingAddress to the attacker contract. Fund the target contract with ETH. Trigger a token transfer that activates the swap mechanism, which will attempt to transfer ETH to marketingAddress using the vulnerable .transfer() call. The transfer will fail due to gas limit, causing revert, but this demonstrates the vulnerability. Alternatively, call Sweep() directly which also uses .transfer().
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy attacker contract with expensive fallback (>2300 gas). 2. Impersonate the owner of MiniDOGE contract. 3. Set marketingAddress to attacker contract. 4. Use deal() to inject ETH into the MiniDOGE contract. 5. Transfer tokens to trigger swap mechanism OR call Sweep() directly. 6. The .transfer() will fail due to gas limit, demonstrating the vulnerability. 7. Contract retains ETH balance (oracle check: address(this).balance > 0).

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is in transferToAddressETH() which uses recipient.transfer(amount) with 2300 gas limit. This is called from swapTokens() when sending ETH to marketingAddress. To exploit: set marketingAddress to a contract with expensive fallback, trigger swap by selling tokens to the pair, and the ETH transfer will fail.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Deploy attacker contract with receive() that definitely consumes >2300 gas. 2. Impersonate owner to set marketingAddress to attacker. 3. Fund contract with ETH and tokens. 4. Transfer tokens to uniswap pair to trigger swapTokens(). 5. The transferToAddressETH will fail due to gas limit, leaving ETH in contract.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Create attacker contract with receive() that burns >2300 gas using storage writes. 2. Impersonate owner and set marketingAddress to attacker. 3. Enable swapAndLiquify. 4. Deal ETH and tokens to contract. 5. Transfer tokens from attacker to uniswapV2Pair to trigger swap. 6. Verify ETH remains in contract (transfer failed).
attempts.failure_reflection: The Sweep() call succeeded because: 1) Sweep() transfers to owner(), not marketingAddress, so setting marketingAddress to attacker doesn't affect Sweep(). 2) The attacker contract's receive() function didn't consume enough gas (only 55 gas used). I need to trigger the swapTokens() path which uses transferToAddressETH(marketingAddress, ...) and make the receive() function definitely consume >2300 gas.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The Sweep() function uses payable(owner()).transfer(balance) which has 2300 gas limit. If I can make owner() return my attacker contract address, the transfer will fail. I can use vm.store() to overwrite the _owner storage slot (typically slot 0 in Ownable pattern).
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Deploy attacker contract with receive() that reverts (consuming >2300 gas). 2. Use vm.store() to overwrite the _owner storage slot (slot 0) with attacker address. 3. Fund contract with ETH. 4. Call Sweep() - it will try to transfer ETH to attacker via .transfer(). 5. Transfer fails due to gas limit, ETH stays in contract.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy attacker with expensive receive(). 2. Use vm.store(TARGET, bytes32(0), bytes32(uint256(uint160(attacker)))) to change owner. 3. Deal ETH to TARGET. 4. Call Sweep() - it will revert. 5. Verify ETH balance unchanged.
attempts.failure_reflection: The test timed out because triggering the swap mechanism involves complex DEX operations that take too long. I need a simpler, more direct approach. Instead of triggering swapTokens(), I should directly manipulate the owner storage slot to point to my attacker contract, then call Sweep() which uses .transfer() to send ETH to owner().
